title: The init-wizard test family times out intermittently in CI, on both ubuntu and windows, and blocks unrelated PRs
summary:
Tests in test/init.test.ts that spawn a process and wait on TTY behaviour intermittently time out in the required 'lint - typecheck - test' job. Seen on both platforms, at both configured timeouts, naming different tests each time:

- 2026-09-11, PR #6, windows-latest: 'cli - init dispatch > the router wires stdinIsTTY + stderrIsTTY + a fake prompter through to the wizard end-to-end (LORE-260)' timed out at 60000ms. It passed on one SHA and failed on the next, where the only difference was a .quest/completed/*.json file.
- 2026-09-15, promotion PR #91, ubuntu-latest: THREE init.test.ts wizard cases (Hermes, Antigravity/Gemini, AGENTS.md-label) each timed out at exactly 10000ms, on a commit that changed only .quest/tasks/*.json, CHANGELOG.md and docs/log.md.
- 2026-09-15, PR #105, ubuntu-latest, run 34984200004 job 104431984958: 'the interactive wizard offers Hermes only when its executable is detected' timed out at 10002.65ms. 3056 pass, 1 fail. The identical source tree had passed that exact job minutes earlier on run 34983645053; the only delta was two .quest JSON files. Cleared on re-run.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A RECORD AND NOT JUST A RE-RUN: it is a flaky REQUIRED check, so every occurrence blocks an unrelated PR until a human notices and re-runs it. Three occurrences are on the books and the judgement that they were flakes rather than regressions has so far lived only in a session's private memory - meaning each new session pays to re-derive it, and one that gets it wrong either bisects a phantom regression or, worse, reports a red job as passing.

THE COMMON THREAD IS NOT ONE TEST OR ONE OS. An earlier version of the rule said 'if it fails on ubuntu too, or names a different test, it is real' - both happened at once and it was still a flake. What actually decides it is the tree: does the diff touch anything the failing test exercises, and did the same tree already pass this job? Two noes mean flake, on any platform.

A 60s timeout on a TTY-wizard test is the shape of a test waiting on something the runner delivers slower, not of a test that is wrong - so raising the number again is the tempting fix and probably the wrong one.

Related: LCLI-491 tracks a different timeout flake (Ladybug projection-lifecycle at 5000ms). Two timeout flakes in required checks may share a cause - runner contention rather than two independent test bugs - and are worth looking at together.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The root cause is identified: why init-wizard tests that spawn a process and wait on TTY behavior intermittently exceed their timeout on a CI runner but not locally
The fix removes the flake rather than raising the timeout, or the timeout increase is justified in writing as the correct model of the work the test does
A re-run of the affected job is no longer part of the normal delivery path for an unrelated diff
The rule for judging one of these failures - does the diff reach the test, and did the same tree already pass this job - is recorded in the repository rather than only in a session's memory
